items.title: Research & Travel Funds for PhD students
items.description: Supports research-related expenses including conference attendance, travel to gather data, and travel to study source material essential for research. Unused entitlement rolls over for up to two consecutive years. Paid on production of receipts. Computer and software purchases are excluded.
items.eligibility_text: All PhD students within their nine terms of research. There is no means test. You may apply more than once in any academic year, providing your supervisor will support your applications.
items.amount_text: Up to £750 per academic year
items.application_method: Download an application form, have your supervisor add written support, and return it to the Tutorial & Academic Office by email or post.
items.evidence_quote: The Committee will grant up to £750 per student per academic year (1st October to 30th September).

items.title: Research Fund for Master's students
items.description: Awards for research and travel, including conferences, for MPhil and other Master's students. Does not cover honorarium payments to research interview participants, or computer software.
items.eligibility_text: MPhil and other Master's students.
items.amount_text: Up to £300 per year
items.deadline_recurrence: Considered each term
items.application_method: Online Research Expenses Application Form, circulated by the Tutorial & Academic Office each term.
items.evidence_quote: Applications from MPhil and other Master's students for awards of up to £300 per year for research and travel, including conferences, will be considered each term.

items.title: Laing Fund
items.description: Supports students from developing countries undertaking fieldwork and research. Covers all categories of expense from visa fees through ground travel, airfares, registration fees, accommodation and board. You must apply in advance.
items.eligibility_text: Open to postgraduate students from developing countries.
items.application_method: Apply using the PhD Research and Travel Application Form.
items.evidence_quote: The Laing Fund has been established to specifically support students from developing countries when undertaking fieldwork and research.

items.title: Welfare Funds
items.description: An emergency fund for a sudden financial shortfall due to circumstances beyond your control — death, illness or job loss of a financial guarantor, or unusual and unforeseeable emergency expenses. Decisions usually within two weeks.
items.eligibility_text: All Postgraduate students (within terms).
items.amount_text: Small grants
items.application_method: See your Tutor, who will discuss the problem with you and endorse the application. The case is sent anonymously to the Student Finance Committee.
items.evidence_quote: Small grants for students experiencing temporary hardship or unexpected costs.

items.title: Book Grants
items.description: Grants towards essential books for research or coursework. Awarded on a percentage basis by formula once all applications are in, so the exact ceiling varies each round. Cannot be used for software or app subscriptions.
items.eligibility_text: All postgraduates within terms.
items.amount_text: Ceiling of £200 or less, typically around 70% of costs
items.deadline_recurrence: Termly; decisions by the end of each term
items.application_method: Termly online application form, plus a single PDF of receipts emailed to grantsawards@newn.cam.ac.uk.
items.evidence_quote: Termly online application form; details will be circulated by the Tutorial & Academic Office via email. Decisions will be made by the end of each term.

items.title: Smart Fund (equipment grants)
items.description: Small termly grants for medical, scientific or other technical equipment for individual use — including clinical equipment such as stethoscopes. Architects are guaranteed up to £300 per year from the equipment funds.
items.eligibility_text: Undergraduate or postgraduate students who pay undergraduate fees.
items.amount_text: Small grants; up to £300 per year for architects
items.deadline_recurrence: Termly
items.application_method: Termly; on production of receipts.
items.evidence_quote: The Smart Fund provides several small grants termly for medical, scientific or other technical equipment for the individual use of undergraduate or postgraduate students who pay undergraduate fees; this includes clinical equipment grants (for stethoscopes etc).

items.title: Instrumental and Vocal Awards
items.description: Awards towards music lessons, made by audition early in the Michaelmas Term. Forms available from the Tutorial Office.
items.eligibility_text: All students are eligible, except those holding Intercollegiate Instrumental Awards or College choral awards.
items.amount_text: £150 each
items.deadline_recurrence: Awarded early in the Michaelmas Term each year
items.application_method: Forms from the Tutorial Office early in the Michaelmas Term; awards are by audition.
items.evidence_quote: The College also offers a number of Instrumental/Vocal awards of £150 each towards music lessons. These are awarded early in the Michaelmas Term.

items.title: Leslie Betts Fund
items.description: A small number of grants for musical purposes — music lessons, active participation in the performance of music, or travel expenses for the latter.
items.eligibility_text: Any resident undergraduate or postgraduate student of Newnham College who is NOT reading for the Music Tripos.
items.amount_text: Normally not more than £90 each
items.evidence_quote: The Leslie Betts Fund provides a small number of grants (normally not more than £90 each) for musical purposes, e.g. music lessons, active participation in the performance of music, or travel expenses for the latter.

items.title: Junior and Senior Music Organiser
items.description: Paid roles organising College concerts with the Senior Music Advisors and the Raleigh Music Society — the lunchtime recital series, occasional orchestral or choral concerts, Music at Advent, and sung grace for the College Feast. Appointments commence in January and run for one year.
items.eligibility_text: Undergraduates and postgraduates are all eligible, except those in their final year or on one-year courses.
items.amount_text: £100 honorarium plus £80 towards music lessons
items.deadline_recurrence: Appointments commence in January each year
items.evidence_quote: An honorarium of £100 is paid, plus an allowance of £80 towards music lessons.

items.title: US Travel Bursary
items.description: A substantial travel bursary offered by the Newnham US Committee for travel to and within the USA during the summer vacation. Winners must write a letter after the visit, with photos and a short video, which is posted on the Newnham website. The source page states the 2026 round has closed but does not give a date for the next one.
items.eligibility_text: Undergraduate or postgraduate.
items.evidence_quote: The application deadline for the 2026 US Travel Bursary has already passed and applicants will be notified of the result in April.

items.title: Completion Grants
items.description: For those writing up their PhDs. The successful applicant is normally expected to complete their thesis within four months of the award being made. Academic progress and any extension funding already granted are taken into account.
items.eligibility_text: Applicants for a completion grant must be beyond terms.
items.amount_text: Up to £1,000
items.application_method: Download and complete the completion grant form and submit it to your tutor, for consideration by the Student Finance Committee.
items.evidence_quote: Applications may be made at any time and should be submitted to the student's tutor for consideration by the Student Finance Committee.

items.title: Kathleen Hughes Memorial Fund
items.description: Grants in aid of research promoting study in the history and culture of the period AD 500 to AD 1200 in Britain, Ireland and Europe. Applications close on 1 June each year. Grants are not made for general maintenance.
items.eligibility_text: Open to all members of the University, but preference may be given to current students.
items.amount_text: Up to £500
items.deadline_recurrence: Applications must arrive by 1 June each year
items.application_method: Send applications to Dr Brittany Schorn (bs321@cam.ac.uk) with details of the project and a statement of any other assistance applied for. Current students should ask at least one referee to write in support directly.
items.evidence_quote: Applications should be sent to Dr Brittany Schorn at Newnham College ( bs321@cam.ac.uk ), so as to reach her by 1 June each year, and must include details of the project for which support is sought and a statement of any other assistance for which application has been made.

items.title: Funds for Language Courses
items.description: Covers half the cost of an optional language course run by the University Language Centre, to a maximum of one course per term.
items.eligibility_text: Postgraduate students taking an optional University Language Centre course.
items.amount_text: 50% of course cost (courses typically £295)
items.application_method: Submit your completion certificate and proof of payment to grantsawards@newn.cam.ac.uk.
items.evidence_quote: We are able to offer grants of 50% of the cost of language courses run by the University Language Centre (typically £295 per course), to a maximum of one course per term.

items.title: Undergraduate Travel Grants
items.description: Funds for travel with an academic or intellectual purpose, or travel likely to benefit disadvantaged people, especially in the developing world.
items.eligibility_text: Churchill College undergraduates.
items.evidence_quote: Funds to support travel that is for academic or intellectual purposes or which is likely to bring benefit to disadvantaged people, especially in the developing world.

items.title: Postgraduate Academic Travel Fund

items.eligibility_text: Churchill College postgraduates.
items.evidence_quote: Support with the cost of travel to present at conferences and medics travelling to undertake electives.

items.title: Sports and Arts Grant
items.description: Financial support for sporting activities, and for musical and drama tours.
items.eligibility_text: Churchill College students.
items.evidence_quote: Providing financial support for sporting activities, musical and drama tours etc.

items.title: Language Bursaries
items.description: Assistance in learning a language not connected with your studies, through the Cambridge University Language Programme. The College refunds half the fees for one CULP course a year.
items.eligibility_text: Any Churchill student.
items.amount_text: Half the cost of fees for one course a year
items.evidence_quote: Churchill College will refund half the cost of fees for one course a year at the University Language Centre under the CULP programme to any Churchill student.

items.title: Music Sizarship
items.description: A paid role overseeing and promoting musical activities in College, liaising with the Director of Music to arrange concerts, chairing the Music Society Committee, and acting as the contact for members wanting to use the Music Centre's facilities. Runs for the calendar year and may be held alongside other music bursaries.
items.eligibility_text: Churchill College students.
items.amount_text: £250 honorarium
items.deadline_recurrence: Runs for the calendar year
items.evidence_quote: The Music Sizarship comes with an honorarium of £250 and may be held in addition to other music bursaries. The post runs for the calendar year.

items.title: Theatre Sizarship
items.description: A paid role fostering theatrical life in College, assisting those teaching English. Offered for one year from 1 January, with the possibility of extension for one further year.
items.eligibility_text: Undergraduates or graduate students of the College.
items.amount_text: £150 per year
items.deadline_recurrence: Offered for one year from 1 January
items.evidence_quote: Churchill College offers £150 per year to undergraduates or graduate students of the College taking on the Theatre Sizar role. The Sizarship is offered for one year from 1st January, with the possibility of extension for one further year.

items.title: Visual Arts Sizarship
items.description: A paid role encouraging the visual arts in College. A large art studio in the garden of 76 Storey's Way is available for visual artwork, drama rehearsals and scenery preparation. Offered for one year from 1 January.
items.eligibility_text: Open to undergraduates or graduate students of the College.
items.amount_text: £100 per year
items.deadline_recurrence: Offered for one year from 1 January
items.evidence_quote: Churchill College offers a Visual Arts Sizarship of £100 per year open to undergraduates or graduate students of the College.

items.title: Bill Brown Creative Workshops Sizarship
items.description: A paid role liaising with the Director of the Bill Brown Creative Workshops to encourage student use of the workshop space and the development of projects using its facilities. Offered for one year from 1 January, extendable for one or two further years.
items.eligibility_text: Open to undergraduates or postgraduate students of the College.
items.amount_text: £100 per year
items.deadline_recurrence: Offered for one year from 1 January
items.evidence_quote: Open to undergraduates or postgraduate students of the College, Churchill College offers a Bill Brown Creative Workshops Sizarship of £100 per year.

items.title: The ISLA Award
items.description: Recognises exceptional achievements by students of Black Caribbean and/or Black African descent, highlighting the talent of Black British students who have been historically under-represented at the University of Cambridge and Churchill College.
items.eligibility_text: Students of Black Caribbean and/or Black African descent.
items.evidence_quote: The ISLA Award recognises exceptional achievements by students of Black Caribbean and/or Black African descent, highlighting the talent of our Black British students, who have been historically under-represented at the University of Cambridge and Churchill College.

items.title: Arthington Davy Studentship
items.description: Awards to cover the cost, or part of the cost, of postgraduate study at any university in the world, for students born in Tonga and of Tongan parents. Preference is given to study or research likely to contribute significantly to the development of Tonga. The Fund's resources permit only a few awards, usually for partial costs.
items.eligibility_text: Students born in Tonga and of Tongan parents, who already have a first University degree and who wish to engage in post-graduate study at any University in the world. The award is conditional on acceptance for the course by the chosen University.
items.amount_text: Partial costs of study
items.application_method: Complete the online form and request that references are sent by the relevant deadline.
items.evidence_quote: Please complete the online form by 30th November 2025 for courses starting in January-July 2026,or by 31st May 2026 for courses starting in September-October 2026.

items.title: G-Research Trinity PhD Studentship
items.description: One studentship for an outstanding PhD student in Engineering, Computer Science and Technology, or Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics, with a preference for machine learning and AI modelling. Covers course fees, a UKRI-rate maintenance allowance and a conference/travel grant, plus career development with G-Research.
items.eligibility_text: Home fee status students undertaking a PhD in Engineering, Computer Science and Technology, or Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics.
items.amount_text: Fees, UKRI-rate maintenance, and a £1,500 per annum conference/travel grant
items.evidence_quote: Conference/travel grant (£1,500 per annum)

items.eligibility_text: Clinical medical students in their fifth year. Preference is given to applicants with a good academic record; both the academic content of the elective and the financial needs of the applicant are considered.
items.deadline_recurrence: Apply by 23 March in your fifth year
items.application_method: Apply online with an outline of the proposed elective, a risk assessment and an estimate of expenses.
items.evidence_quote: Students should apply by 23rd March in their 5th year.
items.title: Harry Barkley Fund for the Year 5 Elective
items.description: A contribution towards the costs of the fifth-year elective period of training for clinical medical students, established from a bequest by Dr Harry Barkley in 1981. Recipients must send a report of up to 400 words about their elective by the end of Michaelmas term of their sixth year.

items.eligibility_text: Clinical medical students in their fifth year whose elective relates to Tropical Medicine or a related Global Health field.
items.deadline_recurrence: Apply by 23 March in your fifth year, via the Harry Barkley application
items.application_method: Same application route as the Harry Barkley Fund.
items.evidence_quote: Students should apply by 23rd March in their 5th year.
items.title: Dinah James Award for the Year 5 Elective
items.description: Applications to the Harry Barkley fund relating to Tropical Medicine or a related Global Health field are considered for a Dinah James Award, established by a bequest from Professor Dinah James, Visiting Clothworker’s Fellow 1975–76.

items.eligibility_text: Undergraduate students participating in sport.

items.title: Girton Sports Awards
items.description: Awards towards the costs of participating in sport. Subscriptions, tournament entries, mandatory kit, transport, playing equipment and travel subsistence are considered; shoes, racquet restringing, Blues blazers, nutrition, sports massage and summer tours are not. Named Sports Awards (Joan McGrath, Robin, Diana Lees-Jones, William and Grace Smith) carry no extra money but mark special sporting achievement.

items.eligibility_text: Undergraduates. There will usually be an academic connection of some sort, though it need not be narrowly course-related.

items.title: General Travel Grants
items.description: For less restricted but serious, educationally beneficial travel outside term, normally in the Long Vacation. Separate from course- and research-based grants for fieldwork and dissertations. Applications are considered as a gathered field, and grants are not given to support holidays.

items.application_method: Standard College grant form.
items.evidence_quote: Students should note applications for this type of language support are normally considered alongside other general travel grants and should apply using the standard College grant form by the deadline of 31st May.
items.title: Language Travel Support
items.description: Support for travel abroad to improve languages. Undergraduates reading Modern Languages or AMES are supported for up to 75% of costs (excluding food), to a maximum of £1,000 across the course; other undergraduates travelling to improve their languages may apply for up to 50% of costs. Not available during the compulsory Year Abroad.

items.eligibility_text: All students undertaking a degree-bearing course. Forms must be counter-signed by a Director of Studies or Research Supervisor confirming the books are academically relevant.
items.amount_text: e.g. £300 across a three-year course
items.deadline_recurrence: Processed four times a year: December, March, June and September
items.application_method: Book grant claim form, available only from the website.
items.evidence_quote: Book grant applications will be processed 4 times a year, in December, March, June and September, with the grant being credited to the students’ next bill.
items.title: Book Grants
items.description: Each student is allocated a sum, depending on course length and year, to purchase academically relevant books — for example £300 over a three-year course. Students are told at the start of each year how much allowance remains. The grant is credited to the next College bill.

items.eligibility_text: Undergraduate members of the College.
items.evidence_quote: travel grants for students travelling overseas for educational purposes
items.title: Travel Grants
items.description: Grants for students travelling overseas for educational purposes, part of a broader set of grants intended to enrich students’ time in Cambridge.

items.eligibility_text: Students distanced from their families.
items.evidence_quote: Recently, the College has also received funding to offer vacation grants , which support students who are distanced from their families with the costs of accommodation over one or more of the vacation periods.
items.title: Vacation Grants
items.description: Support with the costs of accommodation over one or more vacation periods, for students who are distanced from their families.

items.eligibility_text: Postgraduates and undergraduates reading any subject.
items.amount_text: Up to three grants of up to £500
items.evidence_quote: Up to three grants of up to £500
items.title: Downing Enterprise Grants
items.description: Grants supporting costs associated with enterprise projects — an internship, research into a new enterprise, building a prototype, or any other project deemed entrepreneurial. Recipients provide a short report within six months.

items.eligibility_text: Undergraduate students. For Category A you must confirm you have checked what your Department or Faculty will contribute, as some funding is normally expected from that source.
items.evidence_quote: Applications are divided into three categories: A: Academic – directly related/essential element to your current course of study; B: Academically related; and C: Non-academic.
items.title: Vacation Study or Travel Grant
items.description: Reimbursement for vacation study or travel, banded by how closely the activity relates to your course: Category A (directly related or essential), B (academically related) and C (non-academic). Category B applications may be upgraded to the Category A rate if the grant would otherwise cover less than a quarter of projected costs and no other external funding is obtained.

items.eligibility_text: Sidney Sussex students.
items.application_method: Contact the Student Finance Manager (studentfinance@sid.cam.ac.uk) with finance queries.
items.evidence_quote: The College has a range of study grants available to help fund research, travel, or other study-related expenses.
items.title: Study Grants
items.description: A range of grants to help fund research, travel, or other study-related expenses.

items.eligibility_text: Students who have performed extremely well in University or College examinations.
items.evidence_quote: We also award prizes, in the form of money or book grants, to students who have performed extremely well in University or College examinations.
items.title: Examination Prizes and Book Grants
items.description: Prizes, in the form of money or book grants, for students who have performed extremely well in University or College examinations.

items.title: The Academic Fund
items.description: The Girton Academic Resources Fund makes small contributions to academic related expenses, such as College rent when staying out of residence for academic reasons, non-compulsory field trips and dissertation research trips, exceptional dissertation or coursework expenses, and additional CULP language courses. Students should approach their Faculty or Department and other College funds first, and claims are submitted with receipts after the expense is incurred.
items.eligibility_text: To be eligible to apply, you must be an Undergraduate, or a Clinical Medic/Vet student, at the time of the expenditure.
items.amount_text: a maximum of £350 per student per year
items.deadline_recurrence: once a term, with an additional round early in Michaelmas Term
items.application_method: Discuss the application with your Director of Studies first, then apply online using the College application form; the DoS is asked whether they support the application. Claims are submitted with receipts after expenses are incurred. Queries to the Financial Welfare Office (fwo@girton.cam.ac.uk).
items.evidence_quote: The Academic Fund will be open for applications once a term, with an additional round early in Michaelmas Term.

items.title: Language Programmes Fund
items.description: Girton students taking a language programme organised by CULP may request partial reimbursement of the fees from the College. Undergraduate and PhD students may claim for up to two programmes; Master's students may apply once.
items.eligibility_text: Students may request partial reimbursement from their College for the fees, for up to two programmes during their undergraduate and/ or PhD programme. Applicants from Master's Programmes may apply once.
items.amount_text: The current fee is £295 and typically £147.50 can be reimbursed.
items.application_method: Apply online with your completion certificate and receipt.
items.evidence_quote: Students may request partial reimbursement from their College for the fees, for up to two programmes during their undergraduate and/ or PhD programme.

items.title: Enrichment grants
items.description: A pilot fund supporting first-year undergraduate and first-year postgraduate students to take up an enrichment activity separate from their academic studies, such as club and society or sports club memberships, drama, dance or music groups, kit or equipment for those, and volunteering. Academic workshops, field trips, conferences, academic travel, Formal Halls and May Balls, political party membership and language courses are not eligible.
items.eligibility_text: First year Undergraduate and First year Postgraduate students. If the funds allow, this may be opened up to other year groups after Michaelmas term.
items.amount_text: a maximum of £50 in any academic year
items.application_method: Apply online. Applications will be considered on a 'first come first served basis' in the event that the funds run out. Applications to both the Enrichment Grant and Sports Awards for the same sport may not exceed £300 per year.
items.evidence_quote: Thanks to the generosity of donors to Girton College, a new fund is being piloted to support First year Undergraduate and First year Postgraduate students to undertake an enrichment activity.

items.title: Girton College Residence bursary
items.description: An additional College bursary, introduced in 2022, that reduces College Residence Fees for students in receipt of the Cambridge Bursary. The deduction appears on College bills as a discount, for the first two terms in the Lent Term bill and for the third term in the Easter Term bill.
items.eligibility_text: All students in receipt of Cambridge Bursary.
items.amount_text: £21.00 a week from 2025-26
items.application_method: No application: the bursary is automatically applied to eligible students' accounts as a reduction in College Residence Fees.
items.evidence_quote: Introduced in 2022, this new additional bursary will be automatically applied to reduce College Residence Fees by £21.00 from 2025-26 a week for all students in receipt of Cambridge Bursary.

items.title: Girton College Undergraduate Travel Awards
items.description: College travel grants allocated by an annual competition, providing around 35-40 awards each year for travel in the Long Vacation. The proposed travel does not have to be directly related to academic study.
items.eligibility_text: These Awards are generally only given to undergraduates in their second, third or fourth years. Students from other universities spending a year at Girton, and Clinical Vets/Medics, are not eligible to apply. Holders of an award must be students in the academic year (1st October to 30th September) in which the travel is carried out.
items.deadline_recurrence: The 2026 competition will open on 1 February and close on 15 March
items.application_method: Apply online by the closing date with a description of the proposed travel, an environmental impact statement and a completed risk assessment form. Applicants should attend the Risk Assessment presentation as a requirement of their application.
items.evidence_quote: The 2026 competition will open on 1 February and close on 15 March.

items.description: A College music award given to the musician who performs best in the Annual Music Awards Competition. It consists of spending money plus a major grant towards the cost of music lessons.

items.evidence_quote: This award is given to the musician who performs best in the Annual Music Awards Competition. It consists of some spending money, plus a major grant towards the costs of music lessons.

items.title: Choral Scholarship
items.description: Girton awards Choral Scholarships on entry to the College for singers in the Girton College Chapel Choir, which has a programme of services, recordings, concerts and international tours. The Director of Chapel Music will meet prospective applicants and hear them sing in advance of the application process.
items.application_method: See the College's Choral Scholarship application details; you are welcome at a Girton service or rehearsal and the Director of Chapel Music will hear you sing beforehand.
items.evidence_quote: In addition to the Organ and Choral Scholarships awarded on entry to the College, Girton offers University Instrumental Awards, College Instrumental Awards and College Choral Exhibitions to students already in residence.

items.title: Chan and Mok Postgraduate Scholarship
items.description: Open to postgraduate applicants who are permanent residents of Hong Kong, with a preference to those who have studied at schools affiliated to Po Leung Kuk, for a one-year master's course in any subject. The College will also seek co-funding from other University funding bodies to increase the amount of the award, but this cannot be guaranteed.
items.eligibility_text: Open to postgraduate applicants who are permanent residents of Hong Kong and with a preference to those who have studied at schools affiliated to Po Leung Kuk. Available to applicants wishing to pursue a one-year master's course in any subject.
items.application_method: Apply through the University's Graduate Applicant Portal (GAP), ticking 'Yes, I wish to apply for funding' on the 'Funding your study' page and then any scholarships you are eligible for; there is no separate Girton application form. Girton can only consider applicants who applied to the University by the latest date in January listed by the University.
items.evidence_quote: The Chan and Mok Postgraduate Scholarship is open to postgraduate applicants who are permanent residents of Hong Kong and with a preference to those who have studied at schools affiliated to Po Leung Kuk. The scholarship is worth £12,000 and is available to applicants wishing to pursue a one-year master’s course in any subject.

items.title: Hong Kong Founders' Scholarship
items.description: Open to postgraduate applicants in any subject who are permanent residents of Hong Kong. The award is offered for the duration of the course, and the College will also seek co-funding from other University funding bodies to increase the amount of the award.

items.evidence_quote: The Hong Kong Founders' Scholarship is open to postgraduate applicants in any subject who are permanent residents of Hong Kong. The award is offered for the duration of the course and is worth £12,000 per year.

items.title: Maria Luisa de Sanchez Scholarship
